title: だけど — but, however (casual)
summary: A conjunction placed at the start of a sentence to turn the direction: “but / however.” It repeats the previous sentence with だ and adds けど. It is a spoken, casual form of だが and しかし.

patterns.form: だけど／だけれども／ですけど
patterns.gloss: だけれども is slightly more careful; ですけど is polite

body.p: It stands alone at the beginning of a sentence and means that what follows goes against the expectation set by the previous sentence: 行きたい。だけど、お金がない。 The speaker usually shows reluctance, regret or a limit.
だけど is casual. In more polite speech, use でも or ですが; in formal writing, use しかし. Do not confuse it with だけ + ど: it is a conjunction that comes between two sentences.

examples.ja: 行（い）きたい。だけど、お金（かね）がない。
examples.tr: I want to go. But I have no money.

examples.ja: この料理（りょうり）はおいしい。だけど、少（すこ）し辛（から）すぎる。
examples.romaji: Kono ryōri wa oishii. Dakedo, sukoshi karasugiru.
examples.tr: This dish is delicious. But it's a little too spicy.

examples.ja: 手伝（てつだ）いたい。だけど、今日（きょう）は時間（じかん）がないんだ。
examples.romaji: Tetsudaitai. Dakedo, kyō wa jikan ga nai n da.
examples.tr: I want to help. But I don't have time today.

pitfalls: It is casual. In essays and formal speech, use しかし or ですが.
Do not confuse it with the particle けど inside one sentence. Here, it begins a new sentence.
